citation.title: High-throughput charge exchange recombination spectroscopy system on MAST
citation.authors: N. J. Conway; P. G. Carolan; J. McCone; M. J. Walsh; M. Wisse

topic: Instrument design of a multichannel carbon (C5+, 529 nm) CXRS system on MAST, a spherical tokamak, not KSTAR
own_question: How can an upgraded CXRS system deliver impurity Ti and vi profiles with high spatial and temporal resolution from a single spectrometer?
actual_method_and_evidence: The paper describes the hardware: toroidal and poloidal views, collection lenses, 224 fibre channels, a transmission-grating spectrometer, an FLC shutter, a bandpass filter and a four-tap CCD. The authors report readout in under 3.5–4 ms, routine operation at a 5 ms frame period to match 200 Hz Thomson scattering, and about 1 cm radial resolution. Sample profiles are presented. The authors state that time-resolved analysis remains difficult in scenarios with high background emission. The paper includes no quantitative accuracy validation, no latency-to-report analysis and no nowcasting.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: CXRS on carbon impurity lines is an established route to impurity ion temperature and rotation profiles. Modern systems are built around multichannel spectrometers with frame-based CCD readout, for example at a 5 ms frame period on MAST.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: p.2 Abstract/Introduction; p.4 CCD camera paragraph
claim_checks.qualification: MAST instrument only. The frame period is detector cadence, not the arrival time of a processed temperature report. The measured quantity is the C5+ impurity temperature, not main-ion Ti.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Background emission can complicate time-resolved CXRS analysis. On MAST this motivated reliance on heating-beam notches, which supports treating conventional CES reports as processed labels rather than independent truth.
claim_checks.qualification: This is the authors' qualitative statement, not a measured error budget.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Detector readout is under 3.5 ms and the operating frame period is 5 ms. The paper does not report the end-to-end delay of fitted Ti reports.
validation_if_relevant: None quantitative. Sample profiles are shown in a figure that was not visually checked; the Ti and Te overlay is illustrative only.
forbidden_inferences: The source does not show that KSTAR CES reports arrive within 5 ms.
The source does not show that CXRS Ti equals main-ion or physical truth.
The source contains nothing about nowcasting, BES/ECEI or real-time control.
The paper cannot be generalized to all CES systems.
The source does not establish that 1 cm resolution applies to our chord.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional background citation for impurity CXRS instrumentation, detector cadence versus processed reports, and background-subtraction difficulty. It provides no evidence on report timing or estimators.
